judgement.reason: PeerTube supports S3 object storage for videos and PostgreSQL/Redis, so the outcome with changes is acceptable.

reviews.findingEvidence: Unsupported architecture: support/docker/production/docker-compose.yml defines 3 application services (webserver, certbot, peertube). Deployz runs ONE web process per deployment plus declared background workers.
reviews.reason: The webserver and certbot services are an optional reverse proxy and certificate renewer that the compose file says can be removed, so only the peertube app service is needed behind the HTTPS load balancer.

evidence.quote: # You can comment this webserver section if you want to use another webserver/proxy or test PeerTube in local
# You can comment this certbot section if you want to use another webserver/proxy or test PeerTube in local

reviews.findingEvidence: Unconfirmed service: the repository declares redis (redis:8-alpine) in support/docker/production/docker-compose.yml. Deployz did not find how the application uses it.
reviews.reason: The shown lines do not include the redis service definition or the configuration that uses it, so this cannot be confirmed as wrong.

reviews.findingEvidence: Durable local filesystem state declared: VOLUME /data (support/docker/production/Dockerfile), VOLUME /config (support/docker/production/Dockerfile)
reviews.reason: The /data volume holds PeerTube's video storage and /config holds local configuration, and no shown setting moves this data to S3.
